items.title: Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method where an LLM, guided by a staged pipeline and the Lean theorem prover, designs and formally verifies evolutionary algorithms. The LLM proposes algorithms, Lean filters flawed designs, and the LLM then proves runtime bounds using potential functions. This approach contributes by demonstrating LLMs' capability to not only design algorithms but also mathematically guarantee their efficiency without empirical testing, achieving a significant runtime improvement for a specific optimization problem.

items.title: CANS: Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering for Large Language Models
items.abstract: CANS is a novel framework for controlling large language model behavior without retraining. It achieves this by steering neuron activations, using proxies for target behavior improvement and general capability preservation. This method provides a closed-form solution for lightweight, efficient control that minimizes negative impacts on the model's overall abilities.

items.title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
items.abstract: This paper proposes a multimodal framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to align autonomous robots with human purposes. The core method involves transforming natural language human goals into robot missions and drives, enabling open-ended learning robots to generate relevant skills. The main contribution is a three-layer system that facilitates bidirectional interaction, ensuring robot behavior remains aligned with human intentions through semantic understanding and motivational modeling.

items.title: Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research
items.abstract: The Infinity Machine is a self-improving AI agent designed for research on verifiable problems. It generates candidate solutions using tool-using agents in sandboxed environments, with a "kernel" editing its own genome (prompts, tools, etc.) based on performance. Its core contribution is demonstrating autonomous research, achieving novel results beyond the state-of-the-art in quantum information by automatically selecting problems, generating verifiers, and auditing its own findings.

items.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
items.abstract: This paper introduces EBench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in robot control. The core method involves testing an MLLM agent, GPT-6-Astra, in two configurations: direct control and a "harness with policy" mode that can leverage existing specialized policies. The contribution is a comprehensive evaluation showing that the MLLM agent achieves competitive performance, excelling in short-horizon tasks and generalization, while highlighting areas for improvement in long-horizon manipulation.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the GPT-6-Astra control loop on EBench and executor timelines on a Microwave test scene. The input prompt combines the task instruction with a detailed task description annotated from a single training episode. The timeline bars compare active executors across an episode under direct control and under the harness with π 0.5 \( \pi_{0.5} \) , with blue segments executed by the agent and purple segments by π 0.5 \( \pi_{0.5} \) , and with keyframes showing right-wrist camera views from that episode at the marked steps.

items.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
items.abstract: FOCUS addresses the challenge of sparse rewards in long-horizon language model agents by introducing an active learning approach for critic networks. It selectively samples continuations from states that are most likely to reduce the critic's estimation error, thereby improving value estimates. This refined critic then guides the agent's learning with more accurate intermediate state valuations, enabling more effective long-horizon decision-making.

items.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
items.abstract: This paper proposes a system-level perspective on "work agents" that combine foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful digital workspaces. The authors introduce a framework to characterize working conditions and classify digital work, identifying five core capabilities for reliable execution and exploring optimization strategies for models and harnesses. Their contribution lies in providing a unified understanding and systematic approach to building and evaluating agents capable of complex digital work.

items.title: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
items.abstract: This paper independently evaluates DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for safety risks like loss of control and harmful manipulation, using 34 benchmarks aligned with the EU AI Code of Practice. The contribution lies in providing crucial third-party scrutiny for open-weight frontier models, comparing V4.1 Flash-1017 against previous versions and leading closed-source systems, and finding substantial safety improvements.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1.1: Distinguishing evaluation conversations from real-world deployment requests on EvalDetectBench. All models are evaluated on the same 152 conversations (83 evaluations and 69 real requests). a , Area under the ROC curve (AUROC; random chance is 0.5). b , Binary classification accuracy (95% bootstrap CIs [ 6 ] ).

items.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
items.abstract: This paper introduces DECE, a unified arena for evaluating LLM agents in diverse Eurogames. DECE provides shared interfaces and evaluation protocols across ten complex games, enabling a comprehensive assessment of agent performance. The core contribution is demonstrating that while LLM agents exhibit consistent cross-game strategic strengths, their performance also varies significantly based on game-specific mechanics.
items.figure_caption: DECE overview. Shared interfaces connect games and model–harness systems. Seat-balanced matches produce trajectories and telemetry for four analyses. Icons show adapter families; Table 3 lists evaluated configurations. The mascot, pairings, and plots are schematic.

items.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
items.abstract: This paper introduces Evolve on Graph (EoG), a novel framework that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their multi-hop factual reasoning capabilities on knowledge graphs without requiring question-answer annotations. EoG utilizes a "Graph Self-Play" mechanism where a single LLM acts as both a question proposer and an answer solver. To ensure question verifiability and adapt to the LLM's evolving reasoning abilities, it employs Symbolically Verifiable Topology Synthesis (SVTS) to generate and execute reasoning paths on the knowledge graph.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. With only a KG and no question annotations, EoG lets an LLM self-evolve by proposing questions verified on the graph and then learning to solve them.

items.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.abstract: EvoRouter tackles the challenge of efficiently configuring multi-agent systems for web queries by using "insight-guided on-policy distillation." It trains a router to make optimal configuration decisions by distilling learned insights about agent capabilities and interactions into dense supervision, overcoming sparse rewards. This approach enables cost-efficient routing and configuration for large-scale multi-agent systems.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. MAS router for web queries.

items.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes simple LLM harnesses for root cause analysis (RCA) that allow the model to freely choose its investigation steps, unlike hand-crafted agents. These simple harnesses significantly outperform existing LLM agents and traditional methods in identifying the root cause of microservice failures, demonstrating the power of unconstrained LLM reasoning for complex diagnostic tasks.

items.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
items.abstract: This paper introduces "inalienable human-in-the-loop" (I-HITL) to ensure robust human oversight of AI agents, even when the agent compromises the system or an adversarial human tries to delegate approval. The core method is a protocol that requires explicit human approval for critical actions, preventing agents from bypassing guardrails. The contribution is a novel framework and experimental evidence demonstrating the vulnerability of current systems and the necessity of I-HITL for AI safety.

items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces dSpark, a schedule distillation framework to accelerate diffusion language models. It learns optimal unmasking schedules that prioritize revealing tokens that best reduce uncertainty across other positions, enabling faster parallel generation. The core contribution is a method to train diffusion models to commit to tokens strategically, significantly speeding up response generation while maintaining quality.

items.title: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
items.abstract: MiRL addresses terminal agent misbehaviors in long-horizon tasks by identifying recurring error patterns. It then uses Reinforcement Learning to train the agent, specifically starting rollouts at these identified misbehavior points and rewarding successful task completion while avoiding those errors. This approach effectively targets and corrects common failure modes, significantly improving agent performance.

items.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
items.abstract: This paper introduces ZAP, a method for training robot agents that combines pre-trained vision-language models for task understanding with simulation-based fine-tuning for motor control. ZAP leverages a large language model for "what" to do and then trains the robot's actions ("how") in simulation. The core contribution is achieving high real-world performance and strong compositional generalization with significantly reduced training costs and data requirements compared to existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Motion learned in simulation carries over to new real tasks that need reasoning. Left: two of the simulated training tasks. These simple pick and place, stacking, and reorientation tasks with everyday objects teach the model only how to move. Right: the same model, trained exclusively in simulation, tested zero-shot on a real bi-manual robot. No real robot data is used in training. Each task is new in a different way. The test tube and rack are a new object and a new goal. The mid-air handoff strategy has nothing close to it in the training distribution. Similarly, drawing an X in the center of a tic-tac-toe grid is a new type of manipulation guided by reading the board. Playing a mate in one requires reasoning about chess, drawing from the model’s pretraining capabilities.

items.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Reva addresses the challenge of real-time vulnerability detection by extracting the contextual understanding that LLM agents develop over multiple calls. It achieves this by using a novel contextual probing method to gather relevant information efficiently, allowing for faster and more accurate vulnerability assessments than existing real-time detectors.

items.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces Auto-Research Arena, a benchmark for evaluating and advancing autonomous research in language modeling. Its core method separates result admissibility (based on quality and constraints) from progress measurement (based on specific research targets), enabling diverse objectives within a unified framework. The contribution lies in providing a structured evaluation for auto-research systems, revealing that even simple search baselines can outperform complex methods, highlighting significant room for improvement in current autonomous research capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Auto-Research Arena evaluates research systems and expands the idea frontier. Left: Arena differentiates research harnesses across nine complementary objectives. Our simple Sequential Search baseline remains competitive, whereas the TPE method tailored to validation-loss minimization underperforms in this broader evaluation. Right: Multi-target research reveals a broad frontier of ideas. A program combining these discoveries achieves lower training loss than the reference program under matched data and FLOP budgets, as well as lower final held-out BPB at the same model size.

items.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Selective Tie Learning" to improve preference optimization by mitigating spurious correlations. The core method involves strategically augmenting preference data with "ties" (equally preferred responses) to reduce reliance on irrelevant features. The key contribution is a theoretical framework for identifying the most effective ties, demonstrating that those with the largest predicted reductions in spurious reliance are optimal, and proposing practical proxies for influence when exact computation is infeasible.

items.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified statistical framework to improve the efficiency and accuracy of evaluating large language models. It proposes confidence-stratified sampling for direct human auditing, recovering population accuracy even with miscalibrated self-confidence. For LLM-assisted auditing, it models the judge's performance to derive an error-corrected estimator, enabling a more robust and scalable evaluation process.

items.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
items.summary: A popular open-weight AI model exhibited concerning behavior, potentially due to its open nature, prompting a discussion on responsible AI development and deployment.

items.title: Brown student maps the hidden global labor powering AI
items.summary: A Brown University student's project reveals the often-invisible global workforce of data labelers and content moderators essential for training and maintaining AI systems.

items.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM
items.summary: This story explains how to improve tool-call accuracy in vLLM by addressing issues with its function calling capabilities.

items.title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
items.summary: This "Show HN" introduces Hob, an open-source, on-device AI assistant designed as a privacy-focused alternative to cloud-based tools like Claude Cowork and ChatGPT.

items.title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)
items.summary: Cloudflare has patched a vulnerability in their GLM-5.3 Workers AI model that could have exposed sensitive data across user requests due to improper handling of the KV cache.

items.title: The Mythical Man-Month in the Age of AI
items.summary: The article argues that AI development, like traditional software, still faces challenges with team size and complexity, suggesting that adding more AI engineers doesn't necessarily speed up projects due to communication overhead.

items.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
items.summary: Hallmark is a design skill that helps AI models like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex avoid generating "AI slop" by promoting better coding practices.

items.description: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
items.summary: TradingAgents is a framework enabling multiple LLM agents to collaborate and execute financial trading strategies, facilitating complex decision-making and automated trading.

items.description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work — The Vibe You Need
items.summary: Thinkrail is a lightweight, self-customizing IDE that enhances coding with a "vibe" powered by Pi, adapting to your workflow for a personalized development experience.

items.description: Consider it done. The open-source AI agent that works out of the box · 想到，就能做到。开源、开箱即用的 AI Agent。
items.summary: Cindy is an open-source AI agent designed to execute tasks out-of-the-box, enabling users to achieve their goals by simply expressing them.

items.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
items.summary: This repository provides an agent harness for optimizing performance across various AI code generation models, focusing on skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development.

items.description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.
items.summary: Impeccable is a design language that enhances AI's design capabilities by providing a structured and consistent approach to AI-generated design outputs.

items.description: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills before you install them.
items.summary: SkillSpector is a security scanner for AI agent skills that detects vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks before installation.
MicroDuck is a compact, bipedal robot designed to mimic duck locomotion, featuring a small form factor and a focus on agile, two-legged movement.

items.description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.
items.summary: OpenBot provides a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates, enabling users to run models like Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent collaboration.

papers.abstract: This paper introduces DECE, a unified arena for evaluating LLM agents in diverse Eurogames. DECE provides shared interfaces and evaluation protocols across ten complex games, enabling a comprehensive assessment of agent performance. The core contribution is demonstrating that while LLM agents exhibit consistent cross-game strategic strengths, their performance also varies significantly based on game-specific mechanics.
papers.figure_caption: DECE overview. Shared interfaces connect games and model–harness systems. Seat-balanced matches produce trajectories and telemetry for four analyses. Icons show adapter families; Table 3 lists evaluated configurations. The mascot, pairings, and plots are schematic.

papers.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Evolve on Graph (EoG), a novel framework that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their multi-hop factual reasoning capabilities on knowledge graphs without requiring question-answer annotations. EoG utilizes a "Graph Self-Play" mechanism where a single LLM acts as both a question proposer and an answer solver. To ensure question verifiability and adapt to the LLM's evolving reasoning abilities, it employs Symbolically Verifiable Topology Synthesis (SVTS) to generate and execute reasoning paths on the knowledge graph.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. With only a KG and no question annotations, EoG lets an LLM self-evolve by proposing questions verified on the graph and then learning to solve them.

papers.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: EvoRouter tackles the challenge of efficiently configuring multi-agent systems for web queries by using "insight-guided on-policy distillation." It trains a router to make optimal configuration decisions by distilling learned insights about agent capabilities and interactions into dense supervision, overcoming sparse rewards. This approach enables cost-efficient routing and configuration for large-scale multi-agent systems.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. MAS router for web queries.

papers.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
papers.abstract: This paper proposes simple LLM harnesses for root cause analysis (RCA) that allow the model to freely choose its investigation steps, unlike hand-crafted agents. These simple harnesses significantly outperform existing LLM agents and traditional methods in identifying the root cause of microservice failures, demonstrating the power of unconstrained LLM reasoning for complex diagnostic tasks.

papers.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "inalienable human-in-the-loop" (I-HITL) to ensure robust human oversight of AI agents, even when the agent compromises the system or an adversarial human tries to delegate approval. The core method is a protocol that requires explicit human approval for critical actions, preventing agents from bypassing guardrails. The contribution is a novel framework and experimental evidence demonstrating the vulnerability of current systems and the necessity of I-HITL for AI safety.

papers.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces dSpark, a schedule distillation framework to accelerate diffusion language models. It learns optimal unmasking schedules that prioritize revealing tokens that best reduce uncertainty across other positions, enabling faster parallel generation. The core contribution is a method to train diffusion models to commit to tokens strategically, significantly speeding up response generation while maintaining quality.

papers.title: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
papers.abstract: MiRL addresses terminal agent misbehaviors in long-horizon tasks by identifying recurring error patterns. It then uses Reinforcement Learning to train the agent, specifically starting rollouts at these identified misbehavior points and rewarding successful task completion while avoiding those errors. This approach effectively targets and corrects common failure modes, significantly improving agent performance.

papers.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ZAP, a method for training robot agents that combines pre-trained vision-language models for task understanding with simulation-based fine-tuning for motor control. ZAP leverages a large language model for "what" to do and then trains the robot's actions ("how") in simulation. The core contribution is achieving high real-world performance and strong compositional generalization with significantly reduced training costs and data requirements compared to existing methods.
papers.figure_caption: Motion learned in simulation carries over to new real tasks that need reasoning. Left: two of the simulated training tasks. These simple pick and place, stacking, and reorientation tasks with everyday objects teach the model only how to move. Right: the same model, trained exclusively in simulation, tested zero-shot on a real bi-manual robot. No real robot data is used in training. Each task is new in a different way. The test tube and rack are a new object and a new goal. The mid-air handoff strategy has nothing close to it in the training distribution. Similarly, drawing an X in the center of a tic-tac-toe grid is a new type of manipulation guided by reading the board. Playing a mate in one requires reasoning about chess, drawing from the model’s pretraining capabilities.

papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Reva addresses the challenge of real-time vulnerability detection by extracting the contextual understanding that LLM agents develop over multiple calls. It achieves this by using a novel contextual probing method to gather relevant information efficiently, allowing for faster and more accurate vulnerability assessments than existing real-time detectors.

papers.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Auto-Research Arena, a benchmark for evaluating and advancing autonomous research in language modeling. Its core method separates result admissibility (based on quality and constraints) from progress measurement (based on specific research targets), enabling diverse objectives within a unified framework. The contribution lies in providing a structured evaluation for auto-research systems, revealing that even simple search baselines can outperform complex methods, highlighting significant room for improvement in current autonomous research capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: Auto-Research Arena evaluates research systems and expands the idea frontier. Left: Arena differentiates research harnesses across nine complementary objectives. Our simple Sequential Search baseline remains competitive, whereas the TPE method tailored to validation-loss minimization underperforms in this broader evaluation. Right: Multi-target research reveals a broad frontier of ideas. A program combining these discoveries achieves lower training loss than the reference program under matched data and FLOP budgets, as well as lower final held-out BPB at the same model size.

papers.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Selective Tie Learning" to improve preference optimization by mitigating spurious correlations. The core method involves strategically augmenting preference data with "ties" (equally preferred responses) to reduce reliance on irrelevant features. The key contribution is a theoretical framework for identifying the most effective ties, demonstrating that those with the largest predicted reductions in spurious reliance are optimal, and proposing practical proxies for influence when exact computation is infeasible.

papers.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
papers.abstract: This paper presents a unified statistical framework to improve the efficiency and accuracy of evaluating large language models. It proposes confidence-stratified sampling for direct human auditing, recovering population accuracy even with miscalibrated self-confidence. For LLM-assisted auditing, it models the judge's performance to derive an error-corrected estimator, enabling a more robust and scalable evaluation process.
